subproblem.title: Invertible matrix transformations preserve the cokernel
subproblem.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, m a natural number, and D, P, Q square matrices indexed by Fin m over R. If P and Q are units for matrix multiplication, then (Fin m → R)/image(D) is R-linearly isomorphic to (Fin m → R)/image(P D Q), where each image is the image of multiplication on column vectors.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m : ℕ) (D P Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) R), IsUnit P → IsUnit Q → Nonempty (((Fin m → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range (Matrix.mulVecLin D)) ≃ₗ[R] ((Fin m → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range (Matrix.mulVecLin (P * D * Q))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix R, m, D, P and Q with the stated hypotheses. Put V = R^(Fin m), A = P D Q, N = image(D), and N' = image(A). Matrix multiplication on column vectors defines R-linear maps because R is commutative.
2. Choose inverse matrices U and T for P and Q respectively. Thus UP = PU = 1 and TQ = QT = 1. Associativity of the matrix action shows that x ↦ Px and x ↦ Ux are mutually inverse linear maps on V; likewise x ↦ Qx and x ↦ Tx are mutually inverse.
3. Multiplication by P sends N into N'. Indeed, if n = Dy, then Pn = PDy = PDQ(Ty) = A(Ty), using QT = 1. Multiplication by U sends N' into N: if n' = Az, then Un' = UPDQz = D(Qz).
4. Define f : V/N → V/N' by f([x]) = [Px]. This is well-defined: if [x] = [y] modulo N, then x − y ∈ N, so P(x − y) ∈ N' by step 3, and therefore [Px] = [Py] modulo N'. The identities P(x + y) = Px + Py and P(rx) = r(Px) show that f preserves addition and scalar multiplication.
5. Define g : V/N' → V/N by g([x]) = [Ux]. The second containment in step 3 proves well-definedness by the same subtraction criterion. Linearity follows from U(x + y) = Ux + Uy and U(rx) = r(Ux).
6. For every x ∈ V, g(f([x])) = [UPx] = [x] and f(g([x])) = [PUx] = [x]. Every quotient element has a representative, so these identities hold on both entire quotients. Thus f and g are mutually inverse R-linear maps, providing the required linear equivalence and hence its Nonempty witness. All arguments remain valid when m = 0.
proof_key_steps: Choose two-sided matrix inverses for P and Q.
Show P sends image(D) into image(P D Q), using the inverse of Q.
Show the inverse of P sends image(P D Q) into image(D).
Descend P and its inverse to well-defined linear maps between the quotients.
Check the descended maps are mutually inverse on quotient representatives.

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis and matches the independently elaborated one-line proposition. IsUnit P and IsUnit Q use the ordinary matrix monoid, not pointwise multiplication. The bare identifier is unreserved. Steps 1–3 correctly obtain inverse linear actions and both required image containments; steps 4–6 establish well-defined linear quotient maps and their inverse identities on representatives. No cancellation requiring a domain or nontriviality is used. The proof covers m = 0 and invokes neither child nor parent. This independent invariance obligation combines with the diagonal computation by rewriting the supplied matrix equality and composing equivalences; the split is appropriate.
